emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of
August 24, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically
  for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in
  the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should
  indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close
  of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office
  of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2. In Person: The Library Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be open to provide
  members of the public with an opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Open Session Items.

  3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  > On Spectrum Cable Channel 35
  with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.

August 24, 2021

  Inglewood, California
  August 24, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  August 24, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.

  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Jeffery Lewis  Senior Assistant City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  August 19, 2021, in the amount of $513,205.24 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the City Attorney’s Office recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1) Crawford Ministries Inc. & Kingdom Community Development Corporation for
  Right of Indemnity, contribution, and declaratory relief: Hardeman vs City on
  February 29, 2021.
  2) Gloria Godoy Vasquez for alleged personal injury; fall on private property on June
  16, 2021.
  3) Chifontay Griffin for alleged consumer rights violation on January 28, 2021.
  B. Return Late Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 911.2:
  1) Chifontay Griffin for alleged consumer rights violation on January 28, 2021.

  1
   August 24, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-3; and 2) Return
  Claim listed as B-1 for failure to file within time limit prescribed in Government Code,
  section 911.2. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Member Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the Minutes for the Council Meeting held on April 20, 2021, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  AGREEMENT NOS. 21-224, AND 21-225 APPROVED - SOUTH BAY
  WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD, INC. Staff report dated August 24, 2021,
  was presented recommending approval of the attached Non-Financial Work Experience
  Agreements between the City of Inglewood and the South Bay Workforce Investment
  Board, Inc.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement Nos. 21-224, and 21-225. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21 – 138 ADOPTED – APPOINTMENT OF MAYOR JAMES
  T. BUTTS, JR. AS THE VOTING DELEGATE AND COUNCIL MEMBER ALEX
  PADILLA AS THE ALTERNATE, TO REPRESENT THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AT THE LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES. Staff report dated
  August 24, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution, appointing the
  Mayor James T. Butts, Jr. as the voting delegate and Council Member Alex Padilla as the
  alternate, to represent the City of Inglewood at the League of California Cities.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 21-138 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA DESIGNATING MAYOR JAMES T. BUTTS JR. AS THE
  VOTING DELEGATE AND COUNCIL MEMBER ALEX PADILLA AS AN
  ALTERNATE TO THE 2021 LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL
  BUSINESS MEETING.

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 142  PURCHASE ORDER APPROVED - OFFICE DEPOT FOR JANITORIAL
  SUPPLIES. Staff report dated August 24, 2021, was presented recommending approval
  of a two-year blanket purchase order with Office Depot, for the purchase of janitorial
  supplies.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve blanket purchase order in the annual amount of
  $50,000 (total of $100,000). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   August 24, 2021

171  AMENDMENT ONE TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-162 APPROVED – BATEMAN
  COMMUNITY LIVING, LLC DBA TRIO COMMUNITY.  Staff report dated
  August 24, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment One to
  Agreement No. 21-162 with Bateman Community Living, LLC dba TRIO Community,
  extending the term of the agreement through August 31, 2022 (with the option to extend
  for two additional years, in one (1)-year increments), to provide breakfast, lunch, and
  snacks for the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service
  Program (SFSP).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment One to Agreement No. 21-162 in an
  additional amount not to exceed $130,960.60 (total contract amount of $435,173.85). The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – TERCERO, INC. FOR EMERGENCY REPAIRS
  TO THE CITY HALL AIR HANDLER S1 (S1) BUILDING VENTILATION
  SYSTEM. Staff report dated August 24, 2021, was presented recommending
  authorization of payment of the attached invoice submitted by Tercero, Inc. for
  emergency repairs to the City Hall Air Handler S1 (S1) building ventilation system.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $24,775. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-227 APPROVED -
  FERGUSON ENTERPRISES, LLC. Staff report dated August 24, 2021, was
  presented recommending award of a contract and approval of a three-year agreement with
  Ferguson Enterprises, LLC, for the Supply and Delivery of Water Distribution System
  Materials Project, per Bid No. RFB-0134.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award a contract and approve Agreement No. 21-227 in an
  annual amount not to exceed $90,047.64 (total of $270,142.92). The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 21-139 ADOPTED – ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FUNDS
  FROM THE SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS AND
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021. Staff report dated August 24, 2021,
  was presented recommending adoption of a resolution accepting grant funds from the
  South Bay Cities Council of Governments in the amount of $4,999.70, and amending the
  Fiscal Year 2020-2021 fiscal year budget.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 21-139 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, ACCEPTING GRANT FUNDS FROM THE SOUTH BAY
  CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS AND AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
   August 24, 2021

173  ORDINANCE NO. 21-15 INTRODUCED - SALARY ORDINANCE FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2021-2022. Staff report dated August 24, 2021, was presented recommending the
  introduction of the attached Salary Ordinance for Fiscal Year 2021-2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby amend Ordinance No. 21-15 to read Salary Ordinance for Fiscal
  Year 2021-2022. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-15 entitled:

  A ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-
  2022; AND REPEALING ALL PREVIOUS ORDINANCES OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, DOES ORDAIN
  AS FOLLOWS

  which was introduced by Council Member Padilla.

178  ORDINANCE NO. 21-13 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING ARTICLE 7 TO CHAPTER 3 ESTABLISHING
  THE FORFEITURE OF NUISANCE VEHICLES ENGAGED IN IN MOTOR
  VEHICLES SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED. Staff report dated
  August 24, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance 21-13, amending

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 21-13 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY INGLEWOOD,
  ADDING ARTICLE 7 TO CHAPTER 3 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPLE
  CODE ESTABLISHING THE FORFEITURE OF NUISANCE VEHICLES
  ENGAGED IN THE MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS OR
  EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED

  which was introduced at the meeting held August 17, 2021, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  4
   August 24, 2021

 178  ORDINANCE NO. 21-14 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY COUNCIL

  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-228 APPROVED – CELTIS VENTURES, INC. Staff report

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
